title: Evaluation of a Serialized CNF Matrix
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean input word, $B$ a natural number, $r$ a suffix, $varphi$ a CNF formula over natural-number variables, and $	ext{st}$ a machine state. Suppose that deleting the first $	ext{st}.P$ bits of $x$ leaves the serialization of $varphi$ followed by $r$, each of the seven registers of $	ext{st}$ is at most $B$, the length of $x$ is at most $B$, and $	ext{st}.T=	ext{st}.Z=	ext{st}.C=	ext{st}.V=0$. Then the machine can reach the return label with value $varphi$ evaluated under the assignment determined by $	ext{st}.K$ and $	ext{st}.S$, in a configuration obtained from $	ext{st}$ by setting only $P$ to zero. Every configuration before the endpoint satisfies the machine guard and has every register at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: The input suffix after the first st.P bits is the serialization of φ followed by rest.
Every register of st is at most B.
The input length is at most B.
replaced:
For every suffix $r$, CNF formula $\varphi$, and register state $\mathrm{st}$, if
dropping the first $P$ bits of the input $x$ leaves the serialization of $\varphi$
followed by $r$, all seven registers of $\mathrm{st}$ are at most $B$, $|x|\le B$, and
$T=Z=C=V=0$, then the machine can reach the return instruction with the truth value of
$\varphi$ under the assignment determined by $K$ and $S$, with $P=0$ and all other
registers unchanged. Every configuration before the final step satisfies the machine's
preconditions and has all register values at most $B$.
